newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end up in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end up in active trading.

text.p: BOGOTA, June 13 Reuter - Colombian stocks ended up in a session dominated by active dealing focusing on two of the country's major banks.
Bogota's IBB index closed up 0.88 percent at 1,196.21 on volume of about 3 billion pesos. Medellin's IBOMED general price index was up 0.6 percent to 18,125.56 on volume of 4.9 billion pesos.
The buyers were out today and there was a good offering, unlike yesterday when stockholders seemed reluctant to sell,'' a Bogota broker said.
Banco de Bogota, the nation's third largest bank in terms of assets, was the day's biggest winner jumping 2.9 percent to 6.800 pesos per share on volume of 755 million.

Dealers said the bank, the flagship of Colombian magnate Luis Carlos Sarmiento's financial empire, had shown impressive first quarter earnings of 47.6 billion pesos, more than double that of the same period last year despite a 25 percent increase in loan loss provisions.
Banco de Colombia, the nation's second largest bank, jumped 2.49 percent to 411 pesos per share on volume of 851 million. ((-- Javier Mozzo, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944))
